topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, the position of the lecture in the series, and the key learning objectives regarding cancer causation.

topics.label: Endogenous and environmental contributions to cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore what cancer is and evaluate the relative roles of intrinsic biological processes, genetics, and environmental exposures in driving malignancy.

topics.label: Pathogens and infectious agents in carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how viral, bacterial, and parasitic infections contribute to cancer, illustrated in detail by the pathogenesis of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens and mechanisms of DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how various dietary, chemical, and physical agents undergo metabolic activation and induce DNA damage.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, inflammation, and host susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics analyze non-mutagenic mechanisms of carcinogenesis, focusing on the distinction between initiators and promoters, inflammatory microenvironments, and host susceptibility factors.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying and testing carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro methods used to identify mutational signatures and evaluate carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and summary
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by summarising the core themes of environmental risk, the challenges of carcinogen assessment, and everyday risk-benefit decisions.
